chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about salat (prayer) in the resting places of camels and in the enclosures of cattle and sheep. He said: “If you sprinkle it with water while it had been dry, then there is no harm in salat (prayer) in them. But as for the tethering places of horses and mules, then no.”
So this concession is understood as applying to a state of necessity and fear of loss of property, and what clarifies that is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَعْطَانِ: resting places or watering grounds of camels
key_terms.اَلرُّخْصَةُ: a concession in the legal ruling
key_terms.اَلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being discussed
key_terms.اَلضَّرُورَةِ: necessity, the condition under which the concession is understood
key_terms.مَرَابِضِ: enclosures or resting places for livestock such as cattle and sheep
key_terms.مَرَابِطُ: tethering places, here referring to those of horses and mules
key_terms.يَابِسًا: dry, describing the ground before sprinkling

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) allowed in the enclosures of camels, cattle, sheep, horses, and mules?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing salat (prayer) in animal enclosures, permitting it in places for camels, cattle, and sheep if water is sprinkled on dry ground. It excludes the tethering places of horses and mules, and the closing note states that this concession is carried upon circumstances of necessity and fear of losing one's belongings.
